article.story: AMES, Iowa -- — Tre Singleton had 13 points and Jaquan Johnson came off the bench to score 12, helping Iowa State pull away in the second half for a 66-45 victory over Niagara on Sunday. Singleton made 4 of 6 shots and 5 of 8 free throws but he also had half of Iowa State's 12 turnovers. Johnson shot 4 for 6 from the floor and sank 4 of 5 foul shots for the Cyclones (3-1). Cole Farrell sank four 3-pointers and scored 16 to lead the Purple Eagles (0-4). Farrell came off the bench and made three 3-pointers in a span of 3:34 to give Niagara a 14-11 lead. Iowa State battled back to take the first two-possession lead at 22-18 on reserve Taj Manning's three-point play with 7:16 left before halftime. Farrell led all scorers with 13 first-half points and he made two free throws with 2 seconds left to get the Purple Eagles within 32-25 at the break. Manning scored nine to lead the Cyclones. Logan Woods sank a 3-pointer to get the Purple Eagles with 38-36 with 13:34 remaining, but Blake Buchanan dunked off a turnover and Singleton buried a jumper to keep Iowa State in front from there. Iowa State shot 40% overall but went 3 for 15 from distance. Niagara made 33% overall and 25% from distance — 8 for 32. The Cyclones hit 15 of 26 free throws, while the Purple Eagles sank 5 of 8. Iowa State dominated the boards 49-26. Up next Niagara: At Delaware State on Friday. Iowa State: Hosts San Diego State on Nov. 24. ------ Sign up for Top 25 poll alerts here, visit the Top 25 here and see AP’s full men’s basketball coverage here
